definitions.explanation: A name given to someone based on their characteristics, appearance, or other features, often used among friends or classmates.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}のあだ{名|な}は「カズ」だ。
{子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}、{変|へん}なあだ{名|な}をつけられた。
examples.english: When I was a child, I was given a strange nickname.

notes:
あだ{名|な} refers to a nickname — an informal name given based on someone's characteristics, appearance, habits, or a play on their real name. Common among children and close friends.

WRITING:
Usually written as あだ{名|な}. The full kanji forms {渾名|あだな} and {綽名|あだな} are rarely used.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- あだ{名|な}をつける: to give a nickname
- あだ{名|な}で{呼|よ}ぶ: to call by a nickname
- あだ{名|な}がつく: to get a nickname
- {変|へん}なあだ{名|な}: a weird nickname

CULTURAL NOTE:
Nicknames are very common among Japanese schoolchildren. They are often formed by shortening a name (e.g., たかはし → たかし), adding ちゃん or くん, or based on physical traits or personality.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ニックネーム: nickname (loanword, more neutral)
- {愛称|あいしょう}: pet name, term of endearment (more formal)
